Narrative 1: I insisted that a fashion designer sell me her original patented work of art dress because it was a gift I wanted to buy for the queen.
Narrative 2: A fashion designer wouldn't sell me her precious dress, so I waited until nobody was around and took possession of it in the name of the queen.
Narrative 3: A fashion designer wouldn't sell me her original patented dress, so I had a royal dressmaker replicate it in the name of the queen.
Narrative 4: A fashion designer wouldn't sell me her original patented dress, so I had her imprisoned.

Title: All You Can Be
Body: <highest-royal-name> tells you that exciting new opportunities will soon be available to those who have earned it, and then asks what you can be doing to step up your royal game.
Narrative 1: I started a new charity as a way of stepping up my royal game.
Narrative 2: To step up my royal game, I studied vast amounts of history, especially the histories of rulers.
Narrative 3: I went on a humanitarian tour as a way of stepping up my royal game.
Narrative 4: I decided that the best way to step up my royal game was to get some plastic surgery.

Title: Location, Location, Location
Body: You get an email from <other-royal-name> saying <he/she> is looking to purchase a vacation home in America and would appreciate your feedback on which location sounds best.
Narrative 1: I told <other-royal-name> that <he/she> should get an American vacation home in Aspen, Colorado.
Narrative 2: I told <other-royal-name> that <he/she> should get an American vacation home in Miami, Florida

Narrative 4: I told <other-royal-name> that <he/she> should get an American vacation home in Cape Cod, Massachusetts.

Title: Blood Supply
Body: The royal doctor has explained to you that when traveling to places where the blood supply is questionable, you should always carry your own bag of blood.
Narrative 1: As per the royal doctor, I started carrying a bag of my own blood with me when I was traveling.
Narrative 2: Contrary to the royal doctor's advice, I chose not to carry a bag of my own blood with me when I travel. I prefer to travel light.
Narrative 3: I told the royal doctor that it wasn't my responsibility to make sure I had a blood reserve with me at all times. Why did we hire him in the first place?!
Narrative 4: I blatantly ignored the royal doctor after being advised to carry a supply of my own blood with me while traveling.

Title: Fan Least Favorite
Body: A recent poll of your kingdom placed you as the least favorite member of the royal family.
Narrative 1: After a poll of my kingdom placed me as the least favorite royal, I decided to turn the other cheek and count my blessings.
Narrative 2: After a poll of my kingdom placed me as the least favorite royal, I decided to condemn the public for its idiotic opinions.
Narrative 3: After a poll of my kingdom placed me as the least favorite royal, I apologized publicly for my previous actions.

Title: Fan Favorite
Body: A recent poll of your kingdom placed you as everyone's favorite member of the royal family.
Narrative 1: A poll of the kingdom placed me as the favorite royal, but I really didn't care. Those titles are pretentious.
Narrative 2: After a poll of my kingdom placed me as the favorite royal, I thanked everyone for their love and support. I'm nothing without my subjects.
Narrative 3: After a poll of my kingdom placed me as the favorite royal, I wasted no time gloating my success to the rest of the royal family.

Title: Royal Birthdays
Body: A royal advisor is suggesting that you have two birthday celebrations every year, first with the royal family and then the official birthday celebration with commoners. The change would make planning much easier to manage.
Narrative 1: I took a royal advisor's suggestion and started having two birthday celebrations each year, first with my family, and then with the common folk.
Narrative 2: A royal advisor suggested that I start having two birthday celebrations each year, but I didn't want to stop there, and increased my birthday celebrations to a full week.
Narrative 3: I chose not to take a royal advisor's suggestion to celebrate my birthday twice each year. I only need one party, any more is too much.
Narrative 4: When a royal advisor suggested a way to make planning my birthday easier, I decided to just cancel all of my birthday celebrations. It's not worth the time, energy, and expense!

Title: New Menu
Body: Seafood is now being prohibited from the royal family's menu because shellfish has a high chance of transmitting food poisoning.
Narrative 1: Since seafood was prohibited from the royal menu, I haven't gone near the stuff.
Narrative 2: I disregarded an official decree that prohibited the royal family from eating seafood. I couldn't help myself. I wanted shrimp!
Narrative 3: I couldn't be happier since seafood was prohibited from the royal menu. I always hated the stuff.

Title: What's for Dinner?
Body: You're hosting a small dinner party at the palace and need to decide on one more entree option for your high-class guests to choose from.
Choice 1: Chicken tian with fennel and apple salad
Narrative 1: I added chicken tian with fennel and apple salad to the dinner party menu for my high-class guests. They loved it!
Narrative 2: I added ratatouille to the dinner party menu for my high-class guests. They were pleasantly surprised with the meal!
Narrative 3: I added ramen noodles to the dinner party menu for my high-class guests, but they weren't impressed.
Choice 4: Double rib of lamb with bean cassoulet
Narrative 4: I added a double rib of lamb with bean cassoulet to the dinner party menu for my high-class guests. They loved the dish!

Title: Fancy Feasts
Body: <highest-royal-name> has placed a new rule into effect, mandating all of the royal family to attend every meal in fancy attire.
Narrative 1: I dressed to the nines after <highest-royal-name> made it a rule that our family must attend every meal wearing fancy attire.
Narrative 2: The royal chef mistook me for the gardener when I arrived at dinner wearing casual clothing. <highest-royal-name> warned me about my misbehavior.
Narrative 3: I was refused a seat at the dining table by <highest-royal-name> after showing up in sloppy attire.
Narrative 4: I decided to eat in my quarters alone after <highest-royal-name> tried making me dress up all fancy for dinner.

Title: Chair Manners
Body: News reporters have noticed that whenever you're sitting in a public ceremony, you cross your legs at the knee. Such behavior is deemed as 'un-ladylike,' and the media is bashing on you for it.
Narrative 1: I continued crossing my legs at the knee despite the media bashing on me for it.
Choice 2: Cross my legs at the ankles
Narrative 2: I started crossing my legs at the ankles after the media bashed on my 'un-ladylike form'.
Narrative 3: I never crossed my legs again after the media bashed on my 'un-ladylike form'.
Narrative 4: I started sitting with my legs spread wide after some annoying news anchors bashed on my 'un-ladylike form'.

Title: Pick My Fit
Body: You are to appear behind <highest-royal-name> during <his/her> monthly address to the public. There will be a huge crowd, and you know the crown doesn't take appearances lightly.
Narrative 1: I stood dressed in all black behind <highest-royal-name> during <his/her> public address. The crowd could hardly see me there.
Narrative 2: I stood dressed in neon colors behind <highest-royal-name> during <his/her> public address. Everyone in the crowd could see me, and loved the outfit!
Narrative 3: I stood behind <highest-royal-name> wearing nothing but a bathing suit during <his/her> public address. I was escorted off stage at once.
Narrative 4: I decided not to attend <highest-royal-name>'s public address because I knew how fussy everyone was going to be about what I wore.

Title: Pants Please!
Body: The weather is starting to get chilly in <country>, and while the adults apply multiple layers of clothing to warm up, it's customary that boys, aged eight and under, wear shorts at all times.
Narrative 1: I remained true to the crown's customs and suffered through the cold weather wearing shorts.
Narrative 2: I decided to go against the crown's customs and wear pants during the cold months. I was frowned upon.
Narrative 3: Because the crown wouldn't allow me to wear pants in cold weather, I stayed indoors all winter long.
Choice 4: Scream every time I get cold
Narrative 4: Because the crown wouldn't allow me to wear pants in cold weather, I decided to scream as soon as I felt cold. Now we're all uncomfortable.

Title: Strict Vocab
Body: In order to keep up a good public image, members of the royal family are now banned from using the word "<tea/portion/pardon/toilet/lounge/perfume/posh>".
Narrative 1: I immediately stopped using the word "<rb>" after all royal family members were banned from saying it.
Narrative 2: Members of the royal family were banned from using the word "<rb>," but I didn't care and said it anyway. I'm royalty. I'll do what I want.
Choice 3: Use the word behind closed doors
Narrative 3: I started using the word "<rb>" behind closed doors after members of the royal family were banned from using it.

Title: Laced Up
Body: You're running late for an important royal banquet when you discover that your shoelaces weren't ironed this morning.
Narrative 1: I disregarded the fact that my shoelaces weren't ironed and attended a royal banquet anyway. Everything went smoothly.
Narrative 2: I fired the flunky responsible for not ironing my shoelaces. I showed up late to an important banquet because of him!
Narrative 3: I quickly swapped my shoes with a pair that had well-ironed shoelaces. I barely made it on time to a royal banquet.
Narrative 4: I was about to attend a royal banquet when I discovered the laces on my shoes were not ironed, so I swapped them out for a pair of sandals. All those attending the banquet were baffled.

Title: Dinner Protocol
Body: You've been enjoying a meal with the royal family in the main dining hall for about an hour, or so, when suddenly <highest-royal-name> places <his/her> utensils down and wipes <his/her> mouth.
Narrative 1: I continued to feast on the delicious meal prepared for the royal family after <highest-royal-name> had finished. Everyone at the table was shocked that I didn't follow royal protocol.
Narrative 2: I followed royal protocol and stopped feasting on the delicious meal prepared for the family when <highest-royal-name> did.
Narrative 3: While feasting with the family, I noticed that <highest-royal-name> had finished our main course, so I quickly requested that the dessert be served at once. <he/she> loved me for it.
Narrative 4: While feasting with the family, I noticed that <highest-royal-name> had finished with our main course, so I left the table. Everyone was appalled that I would leave before <highest-royal-name>.

Title: Puddle Perfect
Body: While running through the palace grounds in your finest regal attire, you come upon the puddle of your dreams, it's not too deep and sharply reflecting the trees and sky above.
Narrative 1: I practiced restraint by not jumping in a perfect puddle, only because I was still wearing my fancy clothes.
Narrative 2: I couldn't resist splashing in one of the most beautiful puddles I'd ever seen. It was a blast, but I ruined some very expensive clothing.
Narrative 3: I went to fetch some rain boots after spotting the most exquisite puddle. I kept my fancy clothes clean while splashing around.

Title: Sneaky After Party
Body: During an extended royal family event, some of your distant relatives inform you of a plan to sneak into the wine cellar later in the evening. They invite you to the "after-party".
Narrative 1: I snuck into the wine cellar with some distant relatives after a royal family event. The after-party was great fun!
Narrative 2: I decided not to sneak into the wine cellar with some distant relatives after a family event. I wouldn't want to be caught by <highest-royal-name>.
Narrative 3: I warned the guards to keep a watch on the wine cellar after some distant relatives informed me they planned on sneaking in after hours.
Narrative 4: I ordered some distant relatives to be removed from the palace after discovering their plan to sneak into the wine cellar after hours.

Title: Royal Juice-Tasting
Body: You are asked to visit the local harvest festival as part of your official duties. A local farmer insists that you sample her gross-looking <carrot/plum/tomato/broccoli/wheatgrass/mushroom/seaweed> juice.
Narrative 1: I tasted a local farmer\u2019s gross-looking <rb> juice and immediately responded with a loud "eeeeewwwwwww!\u201d.
Narrative 2: A local farmer asked me to try her gross-looking <rb> juice, but I told her I was allergic and offered my sincerest apologies.
Narrative 3: A local farmer asked me to try her gross-looking <rb> juice, so I screwed up my nose and threw it back, claiming it was delicious.
Narrative 4: A local farmer asked me to try her gross-looking <rb> juice, but I "accidentally" bumped the glass with my hip and spilled it.

Title: Show of Fealty
Body: Every year, all noble children must make a show of fealty to <highest-royal-name>. You've been asked to practice your curtsy lest you mess up and trip.
Narrative 1: I was told I would need to curtsy perfectly for <highest-royal-name>, so I practiced every day and pulled it off with grace.
Narrative 2: I was told I would need to curtsy perfectly for <highest-royal-name>, so I practiced a few times and wobbled a bit, but I didn't disgrace myself in front of <him/her>.
Narrative 3: I was told I would need to curtsy perfectly for <highest-royal-name>, but I refused to practice, ultimately falling on my <face/hands/knees/butt> in front of <him/her>.

Title: Show of Fealty

Title: Young Love
Body: A tabloid spotted you <having tea/catching a movie/visiting a theme park/eating at a restaurant/riding horses> with <lover>. The article questioned whether this is appropriate behavior for a young noble.
Narrative 1: A tabloid published a story about <lover> and me <rb> together, and I issued a statement saying that the story was <a lie/a fabrication/deceitful/fake news/misrepresentation>.
Narrative 2: A tabloid published a story about <lover> and me <rb> together, but I ignored the story and let people think what they wanted.
Narrative 3: A tabloid wrote a story about <lover> and me <rb> together, so I called the journalist <insult> on <Twitter/Instagram/TikTok/YouTube>.

Title: The Audacity!
Body: You're in line for the bathroom at school when <classmate>, a commoner, butts you in line.
Narrative 1: <classmate> butted me in line for the bathroom, so I called for <his/her> execution but was denied. How dare they!
Narrative 2: I reminded <classmate> of my rank when <he/she> butted me in line for the bathroom, and <he/she> immediately backed off.
Narrative 3: I pretended I didn't see <classmate> butting me in line for the bathroom and let <him/her> go ahead of me.

Title: Your Biggest Fan
Body: <musician> is on tour and scheduled to play a show in <city>. You'd like to go, but it's already sold out.
Narrative 1: I pulled royal rank and got myself front-row seats to a sold-out <musician> concert in <city>.
Narrative 2: I wanted to see <musician> in <city>, but the concert was sold out, so I went online to ask if anyone would sell me tickets. My act was hailed as "relatable" by the media.
Narrative 3: I wanted to see <musician> in <city>, but the concert was sold out, so I decided to respect the system and just stayed home.
Narrative 4: I attempted to purchase tickets for a concert featuring <musician>, but it was sold out. My response was swift in demanding that <musician> play a private show at my residence within a fortnight, no longer.

Title: The Great Outdoors
Body: Your school is sponsoring a weekend camping trip that you want to go on, but your advisors say you might <fall off a mountain/be attacked by a bear/get lost in the woods/eat poisonous berries/be attacked by mountain men> and die if you go.
Narrative 1: I went on a school camping trip despite my advisors warning that I might <rb> and die. I came back dirty and tired but safe.
Narrative 2: My advisors said I might <rb> if I went on a school camping trip, so I glamped on our estate instead.

Title: In Your Honor

Narrative 1: I agreed to a suggestion posed by <classmate> that our school hold a <rb> party in my honor. The festivities were <magnificent/bumping/lit/splendid/spirited>.
Narrative 2: When <classmate> suggested that our school hold a <rb> party in my honor, I told <him/her>, to <his/her> disappointment, that it wouldn't be necessary.

Title: Dishonor On Your Family
Body: Due to your reputation as a noble who doesn't do your family's name justice, your classmates have started disinviting you to their birthday parties.

Narrative 2: I began crashing my classmates' birthday parties.
Narrative 3: I cried <on my bed/silently to myself/in the closet> after discovering my classmates didn't want to invite me to their birthday parties.
Narrative 4: I decided I was too cool to care when my classmates stopped inviting me to their birthday parties because of my reputation.

Body: You hear a rumor that <classmate> wants to ask you on a playdate to <the ice cream parlor/the movie theater/the jungle gym after school/the playground/the zoo/the ball pit at a nearby fast food restaurant/a local park>, but is too scared <he/she> will be rejected due to <his/her> commoner status.
Narrative 1: <classmate> began inviting me to <rb> every day after school.
Narrative 2: <classmate> seemed distant after I told <him/her> that <he/she> is too far beneath me to hang out with <him/her>.
